examples.ko: 두 팀 감독이 경기 전부터 신경전을 벌였어요.
examples.en: The two team managers played mind games even before the match.
The department head and the section chief had a tense standoff in the meeting.

examples.ko: 가격을 두고 두 회사 사이에 신경전이 심해요.
examples.en: There's a heated war of nerves between the two companies over the price.

examples.ko: 형제가 리모컨을 두고 작은 신경전을 벌여요.
examples.en: The brothers have a little tussle over the remote control.
Before an election the candidates' sparring gets heated.
The mood was heavy because of the tension between them.

explain: '신경전'은 싸우지는 않지만 말이나 행동으로 서로 기싸움을 하는 상황에 써요. 보통 '신경전을 벌이다'로 말하고, 스포츠 뉴스나 회사 이야기에 자주 나와요. 몸이나 큰 소리로 맞붙는 다툼과 달리, 서로 눈치를 보며 긴장을 만드는 데 초점이 있어요.

phrases.example: 결승전 전에 두 선수 사이에 신경전이 벌어졌어요.
phrases.en: A war of nerves broke out between the two players before the final.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신경전을 벌이다'와 짝이 되는 표현이에요. 신경전이 저절로 시작된 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The counterpart of 신경전을 벌이다, with the feeling that the tussle just started on its own.
phrases.en_equiv: a war of nerves breaks out

phrases.example: 계약을 두고 두 회사가 치열한 신경전을 벌였어요.
phrases.en: The two companies waged a fierce war of nerves over the contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신경전이 아주 심할 때 '치열한'을 앞에 붙여요. 보통 '벌이다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 치열한 before it when the tussle is very intense. It is usually used with 벌이다.

phrases.example: 처음 만난 두 사람이 기싸움을 하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The two people who just met are in a battle of wills.
phrases.nuance_ko: '신경전'과 뜻이 비슷하지만 서로 기세를 누르려는 느낌이 더 강하고 구어에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 신경전 but with a stronger sense of trying to overpower the other, and common in speech.

explain_en: '신경전' is for a standoff where people do not fight openly but test each other with words and attitude. The usual pairing is '신경전을 벌이다', and it is common in sports news and workplace talk. Unlike a physical or shouting quarrel, the focus is on building tension while watching each other.

examples.en: That director is a rising newcomer in the film world.

examples.ko: 신예 작가의 첫 소설이 베스트셀러가 됐어요.
examples.en: The young writer's first novel became a bestseller.

examples.ko: 이번 대회에는 신예 선수들이 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many up-and-coming players took part in this competition.
This year's rookie award went to a rising star of the theater world.

examples.ko: 신예 가수 중에서 누구를 가장 좋아해요?
examples.en: Among the up-and-coming singers, who do you like the most?

examples.ko: 그 팀은 신예와 베테랑이 잘 어울려요.
examples.en: On that team, the rising stars and the veterans work well together.

explain: '신인'은 막 시작한 사람이면 누구나 가리키지만, '신예'는 새로 나타났는데 실력이 눈에 띈다는 느낌이 있어요. 작가, 감독, 선수 앞에 붙이거나 '신예로 떠오르다'처럼 뉴스와 기사에서 자주 보여요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '베테랑', '노장'이에요.

phrases.example: 그 신예 작가는 첫 책으로 큰 상을 받았어요.
phrases.en: That up-and-coming writer won a big prize with their first book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 나왔지만 실력이 눈에 띄는 작가를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to a writer who is new but already stands out for talent.

phrases.example: 신예 선수가 경기에서 멋진 골을 넣었어요.
phrases.en: The rising young player scored a great goal in the game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 운동 기사에서 주목받는 새 선수를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is often used in sports news for a new player who attracts attention.

phrases.en: That singer emerged as a rising star this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 주목받기 시작했다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means someone suddenly began to get attention, and it is common in the news.
phrases.en_equiv: to emerge as a rising star

explain_en: '신인' simply means someone who has just started, but '신예' also suggests that the person stands out for their talent. It is often attached before writers, directors and athletes, or used like '신예로 떠오르다' in news articles. The opposite feeling is '베테랑' or '노장'.

en: a disorderly mob; a motley crowd

examples.ko: 처음에는 오합지졸이었던 우리 팀이 이제는 꽤 강해졌어요.
examples.en: Our team, which started out as a rabble, has gotten quite strong now.

examples.ko: 연습 한 번 안 하고 나가면 오합지졸처럼 보일 거예요.
examples.en: If you go out without practicing even once, you'll look like a rabble.

examples.ko: 감독님은 선수들을 오합지졸이라고 부르며 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: The coach got angry and called the players a bunch of rabble.

examples.ko: 오합지졸 같은 군대로는 큰 전쟁을 이길 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't win a big war with an army that is just a rabble.

examples.ko: 모인 사람은 많은데 다들 따로 놀아서 오합지졸이에요.
examples.en: Lots of people showed up, but everyone does their own thing, so it's a rabble.

examples.ko: 오합지졸로 시작했지만 우리는 끝까지 포기하지 않았어요.
examples.en: We started as a rabble, but we never gave up until the end.

explain: 군대뿐 아니라 팀이나 모임처럼 준비 없이 모인 사람들에게도 써요. 조금 비꼬는 말투라서 상대방에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 준비가 안 돼서 우리 모임이 오합지졸 같아요.
phrases.en: We're not prepared, so our group is like a disorganized mob.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직이 엉성하고 모여만 있을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for a loosely organized group.

phrases.en: Without a leader, we turn into a disorganized mob.
phrases.nuance_ko: 질서 없이 모인 무리가 된다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means turning into a group gathered without order.

phrases.en: If we go out without uniforms, we'll look like a ragtag crowd.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 엉성해 보인다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means looking disorganized from the outside.

explain_en: It is used not only for armies but also for teams or groups that gathered without preparation. It has a slightly sarcastic tone, so saying it directly to someone can be rude.

examples.en: That player is an idol to children.
Many fans follow the singer like an idol.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 우상이었던 배우를 직접 만났어요.
examples.en: I met in person the actor who was my idol as a child.
Making an idol and worshipping it is dangerous.
My idol is someone who always makes an effort.

examples.ko: 그 팀은 도시 사람들의 우상으로 불려요.
examples.en: That team is called the idol of the city's people.

explain: 존경하고 열광하며 따르는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 닮고 싶은 사람은 '롤모델'이라고 하고, '우상'은 더 열광하는 느낌이에요. 종교에서 섬기는 조각상도 '우상'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That actor became an idol to teenagers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 사람이 열광하는 대상이 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone becomes a figure many people adore.

phrases.en: I look up to my older brother as my idol.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신이 따르는 사람으로 정한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means choosing someone as the person you follow.

phrases.en: Some religions forbid idol worship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 종교에서 조각상을 섬기는 일을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to worshipping images or statues in religion.

explain_en: Used for a person you admire and follow with great enthusiasm. A person you want to be like is a '롤모델', while 우상 feels more passionate. In religion, a worshipped statue is also called 우상.

t90.ax: That player is an idol to children.

examples.ko: 영화에서 그는 도시를 부수는 파괴자로 나와요.
examples.en: In the movie he appears as a destroyer who smashes the city.

examples.ko: 환경 파괴자라는 말을 들으면 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts to be called an environmental destroyer.

examples.ko: 게임 속 파괴자는 힘이 아주 센 캐릭터예요.
examples.en: The destroyer in the game is a very strong character.
That company is called a disruptor of the market.
They are investigating who the destroyer of the forest is.
Children are little wreckers who break toys.

explain: '파괴자'는 물건, 자연, 질서를 부수는 사람이나 존재예요. 'ㅇㅇ 파괴자'처럼 앞에 대상을 붙여 '환경 파괴자', '평화 파괴자'로 자주 써요. 장난으로 말하면 귀엽게 들리지만, 진지하게 쓰면 강한 비난이 돼요.

phrases.en: He was called a destroyer of the village's peace.
phrases.nuance_ko: '평화'를 앞에 붙여 무엇을 부수는 사람인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 평화 in front to say what the person destroys.

phrases.en: People who cut in line are wreckers of order.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙이나 순서를 지키지 않는 사람을 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong way to describe someone who ignores rules or order.

phrases.example: 작은 거짓말이 신뢰의 파괴자가 될 수 있어요.
phrases.en: A small lie can become a destroyer of trust.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람뿐 아니라 어떤 일이 나쁜 결과를 만든다는 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can also be used figuratively for things that cause bad results.

explain_en: 파괴자 is a person or being that destroys things, nature, or order. It often follows a target word, as in 환경 파괴자 or 평화 파괴자. Said jokingly it can sound cute, but said seriously it is a strong accusation.

examples.en: I'm still a rookie who isn't good at the job yet.
I made a lot of mistakes when I was a newbie.

examples.ko: 풋내기라고 해도 열정은 누구에게도 지지 않아요.
examples.en: Even though I'm a novice, I'm second to none in passion.
Though a rookie, the player stayed calm in the game.
A greenhorn reporter landed a big scoop.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 풋내기들이 많아서 분위기가 밝아요.
examples.en: Our team has many newcomers, so the mood is bright.

explain: '초보자'보다 경험이 적고 서툴러 보이는 사람이라는 느낌이 있어서, 남이 말하면 얕잡아 보는 말처럼 들릴 수 있어요. 자기 자신을 낮춰 말할 때는 괜찮아요. 중립적으로 말하려면 '초보', '신입'을 쓰세요.

phrases.en: I'm still a beginner driver.
phrases.nuance_ko: '풋내기'보다 중립적이라 남에게도 편하게 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More neutral than 풋내기, so it's fine to use about other people.

phrases.en: I'm new here, so there's a lot I don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 모임에 새로 들어온 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone newly joined to a company or group.

phrases.en: I'm still a novice, so I have a lot to learn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기 자신을 낮춰 말할 때 자연스러운 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural conjugated form when humbly describing yourself.

explain_en: Compared with '초보자', it suggests someone with little experience who looks unskilled, so it can sound belittling when others say it. It is fine for describing yourself modestly. For a neutral tone, use '초보' or '신입'.

examples.en: The war created many evacuees.
The evacuees are staying in temporary shelters.
The school became a shelter for evacuees.
Volunteers handed out blankets to the evacuees.
Some evacuees lost their homes in the flood.

examples.ko: 피난민 아이들이 새 학교에 다니기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The evacuee children started attending a new school.

explain: 전쟁이나 재난의 위험을 피해 살던 곳을 떠난 사람에게 써요. 나라 밖으로 피한 사람은 '난민'을 더 많이 써요. 홍수나 지진으로 집을 잃은 사람은 '이재민'이라고도 해요. 한국전쟁 이야기에도 '피난민'이 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The flood created many evacuees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재난이나 전쟁 뒤에 사람들이 떠나게 되었다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means people were forced to leave after a disaster or war.

phrases.en: Volunteers help the evacuees.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움이나 구호 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common in talk about aid and relief.

phrases.en: My grandfather was a war refugee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일 때문에 피난한 사람인지 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: The cause of fleeing is put in front.

explain_en: People escaping a disaster or war, focus on the flight itself. It refers to people who left home to escape the danger of war or disaster. For people who fled abroad, '난민' is used more. People who lost homes to floods or earthquakes are also called '이재민'. '피난민' often appears in stories about the Korean War.

examples.ko: 이번 달에 가욋돈이 생겨서 친구한테 밥을 샀어요.
examples.en: I got some extra money this month, so I bought my friend a meal.
I work a part-time job on weekends to earn some extra money.

examples.ko: 월급 말고 가욋돈이 조금 있으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I wish I had a little extra money besides my salary.
I won't spend the extra money; I'll save it.
I'm slowly saving up some extra money from a side job.
It was money I never expected, so I felt great.

explain: 월급처럼 정해진 돈 말고 따로 생긴 돈을 말해요. '부수입'과 비슷하지만 '가욋돈'이 더 편한 말투예요. '가외'와 '돈' 사이에 ㅅ이 들어가는 표기에 주의하고, 발음은 [가왼똔]이에요.

phrases.en: I got some extra money, so I bought a present.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상 밖의 돈이 생겼을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when unexpected extra money comes in.

phrases.en: I spent all the extra money instead of saving it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 생활비가 아닌 돈을 쓸 때 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for spending money outside the regular budget.

phrases.en: I earned a little side income.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가욋돈'과 비슷하지만 조금 더 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 'gaoetdon' but a bit more formal.

explain_en: It means money you get on top of a fixed amount like a salary. It is similar to '부수입' but has a more casual feel. Note the spelling with an inserted ㅅ between '가외' and '돈', and the pronunciation is [가왼똔].

examples.en: You should be careful with investments that promise high returns.

examples.ko: 고수익 아르바이트라는 광고는 일단 의심해 보세요.
examples.en: Be suspicious of ads for high-paying part-time jobs at first.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 고수익 사업에 집중하고 있어요.
examples.en: This company is focusing on high-profit businesses.
If you want high profits, the risk is just as big.
Many people are looking for high-income jobs.
He works as a high-earning freelancer.

explain: 반대말은 '저수익'이에요. '고수익 보장' 같은 광고 문구에 자주 나오는데, 이런 말은 사기일 수도 있어서 조심하라는 이야기를 많이 해요.

phrases.example: 그 가게는 요즘 고수익을 올리고 있어요.
phrases.en: That shop is making high profits these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 많이 번다는 뜻으로 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means earning a lot, used in news and business talk.

phrases.example: 고수익 보장이라는 말은 믿으면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You shouldn't trust claims of guaranteed high profits.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광고 문구로 자주 보이는데 조심하라는 이야기와 함께 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common ad phrase, often mentioned with warnings.

phrases.en: Even if the profit is low, a safe investment is better.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고수익'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 고수익.

explain_en: The opposite is '저수익' (low profit). It often appears in ads like '고수익 보장' (high profit guaranteed), and people often warn that such claims may be scams.

examples.ko: 돈푼이나 모았다고 사람을 무시하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't look down on people just because you've saved a bit of money.

examples.ko: 겨우 돈푼 때문에 친구랑 싸우지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't fight with a friend over a measly bit of money.
He struts around because he has a little money.
I bought a gift with the little money I made from my part-time job.

examples.ko: 돈푼 좀 쥐여 줬더니 금세 좋아하더라고요.
examples.en: I slipped him a little cash and he cheered up right away.
I set off on a trip without a penny.

explain: 많지 않은 돈이나 약간의 돈을 가볍게, 때로는 비꼬듯이 말할 때 써요. '돈푼깨나', '돈푼이나'처럼 '돈이 좀 있는 사람'을 비꼬는 표현으로 자주 나와요. 정중한 자리에서는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: Don't show off just because you earn a little money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금 있는 돈을 가볍게 말하며 비꼴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used sarcastically for someone who has a bit of money.

phrases.en: He looks down on people just because he has some money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '돈이 좀 있는' 사람을 비꼬는 표현으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A frequent expression to mock someone who is somewhat well-off.

phrases.en: It's sad when family members fight over a little money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작은 돈 때문에 일이 벌어졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something happens over a small amount of money.

explain_en: It refers to a small or modest amount of money in a casual, sometimes sarcastic way. It often appears as '돈푼깨나' or '돈푼이나' to mock people who have a bit of money. It's not used in polite settings.

examples.ko: 컵라면에 뜨거운 물을 들이부은 다음 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I poured hot water into the instant noodles and waited.

examples.ko: 그는 새 사업에 돈을 너무 많이 들이부었어요.
examples.en: He poured far too much money into his new business.

examples.ko: 물을 한꺼번에 들이부으면 흙이 쓸려 가요.
examples.en: If you pour all the water in at once, the soil gets washed away.
Outside, the rain is pouring down as if from a bucket.

examples.ko: 이 게임에 시간을 들이붓는 사람이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: Lots of people pour their time into this game.

examples.ko: 아이 교육에 월급을 전부 들이부어도 부족해요.
examples.en: Even if I pour my whole salary into my child's education, it's not enough.

explain: '붓다'에 '들이-'가 붙어서 물이나 돈을 거침없이 많이 쏟아 넣는 느낌이 있어요. 돈·시간·노력을 아낌없이 쏟을 때도 비유로 써요. 'ㅅ 불규칙'이라서 '들이부어요, 들이부었어요'로 바뀌어요.

phrases.en: I poured my time and effort into that work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '들이붓다'와 비슷하고, 시간·돈·노력을 아낌없이 쓸 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '들이붓다', often used for spending time, money and effort freely.

phrases.example: 그 가게에 돈을 너무 많이 들이부었어요.
phrases.en: I put too much money into that shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아낌없이 많은 돈을 쓴다는 뜻으로 쓰는 비유적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative pairing meaning to spend a large amount of money freely.

phrases.example: 화분에 물을 한꺼번에 들이부어서 바닥이 젖었어요.
phrases.en: I poured water into the flowerpot all at once, so the floor got wet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅅ 불규칙'이라서 '-아/어서'가 붙으면 '들이부어서'가 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because it is a ㅅ-irregular verb, '-아/어서' makes it '들이부어서'.

explain_en: Pouring forcefully or in large amounts, all at once. The '들이-' prefix on '붓다' gives a feel of pouring something in a lot, without holding back. It is also used figuratively for pouring money, time or effort into something. It is a 'ㅅ-irregular' verb, so it becomes '들이부어요' and '들이부었어요'.

examples.en: This bag isn't real; it's an imitation.

examples.ko: 시장에서 산 시계가 모조품인 걸 나중에 알았어요.
examples.en: I found out later that the watch I bought at the market was a fake.
The museum only displays replicas of the relics.
You have to be careful with sites that sell counterfeits.

examples.ko: 연극 소품으로 쓸 모조품 왕관을 만들었어요.
examples.en: I made a replica crown to use as a prop in the play.
Even though it's an imitation, I like it because the design is pretty.

explain: 반대말은 '진품'이에요. 박물관의 복제품처럼 나쁜 뜻이 없을 때도 쓰지만, 일상 대화에서 가짜 상품을 편하게 말할 때는 '짝퉁'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I unknowingly bought an imitation while traveling.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가짜 물건을 산 경우에 가장 자연스럽게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing when someone bought a fake item.

phrases.en: It's hard to tell the genuine article from the imitation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 반대말 '진품'과 함께 비교할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the opposite word 진품 for comparison.

phrases.en: This watch is a knockoff, so it is cheap.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 가짜 상품을 편하게 말하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday word for fake goods.

explain_en: Fake copy of a branded item; physical product (시장에서 산 가방) Its opposite is '진품' (genuine article). It can be neutral, like museum replicas, but in casual talk about fake goods people say '짝퉁'.

t90.ax: This bag isn't real; it's an imitation.

examples.en: A platinum ring is harder and rarer than gold.
We had our wedding rings made in platinum.
This necklace has diamonds set in platinum.

examples.ko: 백금은 변하지 않아서 오래 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Platinum does not tarnish, so you can use it for a long time.

examples.ko: 백금 가격이 올라서 반지 값도 올랐어요.
examples.en: The price of platinum went up, so the ring price rose too.
The factory uses platinum as a catalyst.

explain: 은빛이 도는 하얀 귀금속으로, 변색이 거의 없어요. '화이트골드'는 금에 다른 금속을 섞은 것이라 백금과 달라요. 한국에서는 '플래티넘'이라고도 하고, 시상이나 등급에도 써요.

phrases.example: 백금 반지는 오래 써도 색이 안 변해요.
phrases.en: A platinum ring doesn't change color even after long use.
phrases.nuance_ko: 백금이 들어간 장신구를 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for jewelry made of platinum.

phrases.en: This necklace is made of platinum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 말할 때 '(으)로'를 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '(으)로' after the word to state the material.

phrases.en: This card is platinum grade.
phrases.nuance_ko: 같은 말이지만 '플래티넘'은 카드나 상의 등급 이름에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same thing, but '플래티넘' is more common in card or award tier names.

explain_en: A silvery-white precious metal that barely tarnishes. 화이트골드 is gold mixed with other metals and is different from 백금. Koreans also say 플래티넘, which is used for awards and membership grades too.

examples.ko: 회장이 비자금을 만든 사실이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The news reported that the chairman had built a slush fund.

examples.ko: 아내 몰래 비자금을 모으는 남편 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a story about a husband secretly saving up a stash of money behind his wife's back.
An investigation began because of suspicions about a slush fund.
I saved my allowance and made a small secret stash.

examples.ko: 회사 돈으로 비자금을 조성하는 건 불법이에요.
examples.en: Creating a slush fund with company money is illegal.
An old secret stash of money turned up in the wardrobe.

explain: 뉴스에서는 회사나 정치인이 몰래 만든 불법 자금을 말할 때 '비자금 조성'이라고 많이 써요. 일상에서는 가족 몰래 모아 둔 개인 돈을 가볍게 말하기도 해요. '비자금을 만들다/모으다/조성하다'로 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 비자금을 만들어서 문제가 됐어요.
phrases.en: That company made a slush fund, which became a problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몰래 돈을 따로 마련할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for secretly setting money aside.

phrases.en: A slush fund case was in the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal phrase often seen in the news.

phrases.en: He hid his secret money from his wife.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몰래 모은 돈을 감출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for hiding secretly saved money.

explain_en: In the news, '비자금 조성' refers to illegal funds that a company or politician secretly builds up. In daily life it can also lightly refer to personal money that someone secretly saves from their family. It is often used as '비자금을 만들다/모으다/조성하다'.
